questions.question_text: Choose the correct synonym for 'Resilient'.
questions.explanation: Resilient means the ability to recover quickly from difficulties, similar to being adaptable.

questions.question_text: Identify the grammatically correct sentence.
questions.explanation: The subject 'she' requires the singular auxiliary verb 'does' with 'not' (doesn't), followed by the base verb 'like'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct antonym for 'Benevolent'.
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly; malicious means intending to do harm.

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence with the correct punctuation.
options: He, ran to the store but forgot his wallet.
He ran to the store, but he forgot his wallet.
He ran to the store but, forgot his wallet.
He ran, to the store, but forgot his wallet.
questions.explanation: A comma is used before a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses.

questions.question_text: Complete the sentence: 'Neither the manager nor the employees ___ aware of the policy change.'
questions.explanation: In 'neither/nor' sentences, the verb agrees with the closer subject (employees, plural).

questions.question_text: Choose the correct preposition: 'She has been working here ___ 2015.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used to specify a starting point in time.

questions.question_text: Select the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling of the word is 'Accommodation' (double c, double m).

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'A blessing in disguise'?
options: A good thing that seemed bad at first
questions.explanation: An idiom referring to a misfortune that eventually results in something good happening later.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: 'The report ___ by the committee yesterday.'
questions.explanation: The sentence is in passive voice and refers to a completed past action.

questions.question_text: Choose the best word to complete the sentence: 'His ___ attempt to win the race was unsuccessful.'
questions.explanation: Futile means incapable of producing any useful result; pointless.

questions.question_text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'The team reached a ___ agreement after hours of debate.'
questions.explanation: Unanimous means fully in agreement, which fits the context of resolving a debate.

questions.question_text: Identify the passive voice version of: 'The chef prepared the meal.'
options: The meal is prepared by the chef.
The meal was prepared by the chef.
The meal has been prepared by the chef.
The chef is preparing the meal.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in past simple tense, so the passive version must maintain that tense.

questions.question_text: Select the correct usage of 'affect' vs 'effect': 'The new regulations will ___ our production line.'
questions.explanation: Affect is typically a verb meaning to influence or produce a change.

questions.question_text: Choose the synonym for 'Ephemeral'.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral refers to something lasting for a very short time.

questions.question_text: Correct the sentence: 'Me and him went to the store.'
options: Him and I went to the store.
He and I went to the store.
Me and he went to the store.
Him and me went to the store.
questions.explanation: Subject pronouns (He, I) must be used instead of object pronouns (Him, Me) when performing the action.

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'To burn the midnight oil'?
options: To work late into the night
questions.explanation: This idiom refers to working or studying late into the night.

questions.question_text: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Each of the students have finished their work.
Each of the students has finished their work.
The students has finished their work.
Every student have finished their work.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is a singular subject and requires the singular verb 'has'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct preposition: 'He is interested ___ learning new business software.'
questions.explanation: The standard preposition used with the adjective 'interested' is 'in'.

questions.question_text: What is the antonym of 'Ambiguous'?
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation; clear means easily understood.

questions.question_text: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling requires double 'c' and double 'm'.
